- This is a hybrid position requiring 3 days per week in our San Francisco, CA headquarter office and 2 days working remotely. Relocation and housing assistance will be included as part of the co-op.

About this role:

Samsara’s cloud-connected sensor platform collects observations about the world in near real-time. Samsara builds an extensive set of products, including battery-powered, wireless sensors, linux-based IoT gateways, and Internet-connected dashcams. These devices are the building blocks Samsara uses to construct enterprise solutions for a wide range of verticals, including commercial fleet management and industrial monitoring. Through a unique integration of sensor data such as GPS, acceleration, temperature, video, and more, we enable our customers to gain greater insights into operations, identify and eliminate inefficiencies, and react to alerts all in near real-time.

As a firmware engineering intern-MCU at Samsara, you will develop software that runs on millions of devices, deployed by our industrial and enterprise customers. You’ll tackle challenges including evaluating and selecting hardware components, bringing up new hardware platforms and sensors, building systems to gather data and detect meaningful events, and structuring recorded data to allow efficient analysis across thousands of devices while providing deep insights into individual events.

You should apply if:

- You want to impact the industries that run our world: The software, firmware, and hardware you build will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

- You want to build for scale: With over 2.3 million IoT devices deployed to our global customers, you will work on a range of new and mature technologies driving scalable innovation for customers across industries driving the world's physical operations.

- You are a life-long learner: We have ambitious goals. Every Samsarian has a growth mindset as we work with a wide range of technologies, challenges, and customers that push us to learn on the go.

- You believe customers are more than a number: Samsara engineers enjoy a rare closeness to the end user and you will have the opportunity to participate in customer interviews, collaborate with customer success and product managers, and use metrics to ensure our work is translating into better customer outcomes.

- You are a team player: Working on our Samsara Engineering teams requires a mix of independent effort and collaboration. Motivated by our mission, we’re all racing toward our connected operations vision, and we intend to win together.

In this role, you will:

- Collaborate with other firmware engineers on the team to design, develop and maintain embedded software for our gateway and sensor products

- Bring up new hardware platforms: configuring I/O, debugging interfaces such as SPI, I2C, UART, CAN and ADC, testing connectivity, validating design and debugging system initialization

- Implement peripheral drivers, secure bootloaders and device firmware update, core management layers (power manager, connectivity manager, etc)

- Design protocols and implement efficient hardware management to optimize energy consumption of battery powered sensors and gateways

- Work cross-functionally with different stakeholders across product, full-stack and quality teams to deliver reliable high quality embedded software

- Gain hands on experience in a fast-paced and innovative environment

- Get valuable mentorship and guidance from experienced firmware engineers

- Be exposed to the entire product development lifecycle, from concept to deployment

Requirements for the role:

- Enrolled in a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field .

- Must have solid C programming skills

- Familiarity with embedded programming concepts

- Prior experience with MCU development environments and tools (Segger J-Link, GCC)

- Experience working in bare metal and RTOS-based systems such as Zephyr and/or FreeRTOS

- Experience in one or more core technologies such as BLE, GPS, LTE and CAN

- Strong problem-solving skills and an analytical mindset to debug and optimize code.

- Be excited about sensors, connectivity protocols, distributed systems, and their application to solve real world problems

- Thrive in an environment that requires rapid deployment and product iteration based on customer feedback while focusing on automated testing and code quality

- Any prior projects, coursework, or personal projects related to embedded systems and firmware development would be advantageous.

At Samsara, we welcome all. All sizes, colors, cultures, sexes, beliefs, religions, ages, people. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems. $38—$58 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About The Supplier Industrialization Engineering Team

Zipline is scaling drone production and flight operations by more than 20× over the next three years while maintaining best-in-class safety and reliability. You will own the entire supplier industrialization and supplier development engineering functions — building the team, processes, tools, and culture that make Zipline’s massive scale-up possible without compromising quality, delivery, or cost.

The Role

As an SIE Intern, the projects you undertake will be focused on the improvement of manufacturing operations & quality at critical Zipline suppliers. This involves working with internal & external cross-functional stakeholders on design for manufacturing & assembly, manufacturing process design & implementation, statistical quality control, and root cause analysis to ensure that Zipline suppliers can meet quality, cost & delivery targets set for them.

What You'll Do

- Design for X (DfX) Discussions: Participate in DfX discussions with internal and external stakeholders to ensure designs are optimized for manufacturability, assembly, and efficiency across Zipline’s Top Level Assemblies (TLAs) and sub-assemblies.

- Assembly Line Management: Assist with the planning, budgeting, design, procurement, commissioning, and validation of assembly lines and associated equipment at Zipline for Product Validation Builds and mass production at contract manufacturers (CMs).

- Process Documentation & Training: Develop and maintain key process documentation such as Manufacturing Process Flows, FMEAs, Control Plans, and Work Instructions. Provide training to operators and quality teams to ensure consistent standards in manufacturing and assembly processes.

- Supplier Management & Qualification: Support in evaluating and qualifying new suppliers, ensuring they meet Zipline’s quality and production standards. Assist in implementing manufacturing processes at supplier facilities to meet the Zipline Approval Process (ZAP) requirements.

- Fixture Design & Automation: Design fixtures for assembly and inspection, and propose automation strategies to improve efficiency and reliability, both at Zipline and supplier facilities.

- Root Cause Analysis (RCA) & Corrective Actions: Assist in performing root cause analysis and implementing corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) to resolve quality issues, ensuring these actions are effectively implemented to prevent future occurrences.

- Supplier and Process Performance Tracking: Monitor and track Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) such as first-pass yield, on-time delivery, and cost of poor quality, generating regular reports for internal and external stakeholders to drive continuous improvements.

- Continuous Improvement Projects: Assist in Continuous Improvement (CI) projects to enhance manufacturing processes, reduce costs, and improve product quality at both Zipline and its supplier locations

What You'll Bring

- Must have at least completed the second year of your Undergraduate studies. Masters and PhD students are also eligible.

- Proficiency in 3D CAD Software (NX preferred) & ability to read Engineering Drawings (with GD&T)

- Understanding of traditional & non-traditional manufacturing processes (Machining, Injection Molding, Sheet Metal Stamping, 3D Printing, PCBA Manufacturing, Mechanical or Electromechanical Assembly, etc.)

- Understanding of Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) & Production Part Approval Process (PPAP)

- Understanding of Problem Solving Frameworks (8D, FTA, Pareto Analysis, etc.) & RCA/ CAPA Techniques used within these frameworks

- Willingness to work in a super fast-paced environment that is in a constant state of evolution

- Pursuing a degree in one of the following concentrations: Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, Statistics, Mathematics.

What Else You Should Know

Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January to April/May.

The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.

The Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) group engineers solutions from concept design to field deployment for our government sponsors on rapid timelines. What to Expect

Heron Power is a startup company building cutting-edge power electronics for the 21st-century grid. We aim to de-bottleneck the growth of electricity generation and consumption with scalable, innovative, and less costly hardware solutions, accelerating the electrification of everything.

Our first goal is to build better converters (inverters & rectifiers) to connect large-scale renewables, storage, and loads to the grid. Heron’s leadership team is made up of seasoned veterans who have designed and shipped gigawatts of power conversion products over the past decade.

We understand that no one individual knows everything. We will all learn a lot together and from each other. We strive to build a collaborative, enriching environment conducive to personal, technical, and career growth. You can expect to work in a dynamic environment, driven by first principles engineering, solving difficult problems—with a strong bias toward hands-on execution and learning by doing.

Job Overview

You will build and operate the test infrastructure we use to validate grid-tied converters. This role owns a meaningful slice of the development loop: test bench design and build, test execution, data analysis, failure isolation, and verified fixes. You will uncover real design and process failures by running physical tests and building automated equipment and data workflows. We prioritize a strong foundation in first principles, practical skill, and a bias toward getting things done. We care as much about how you work as what you already know.

How You Will Contribute

Test Bench Architecture & Build

- Design and build electrical reliability test benches for power electronics hardware—inverters, DC/DC converters, bi-directional power stages.

- Specify, procure, and integrate lab equipment: programmable power supplies, electronic loads, DAQ systems, sensors, protection hardware, interlocks, and cabling.

- Own the bench system design: grounding, measurement integrity, EMI-aware instrumentation, protection strategy, safe operating procedures, and maintainability.

Software & Test Automation

- Contribute to our software test infrastructure for system integration and reliability testing — test architecture, hardware abstraction layers, and result reporting pipelines.

- Write software tests that interact directly with hardware and firmware over CAN, UART, Modbus, TCP/IP — debugging signal integrity, protocol failures, and firmware edge cases.

- Write concurrent, fault-tolerant software for our next-generation manufacturing test platform: Firmware Flashing, FCT, EOL stations running autonomously on the factory floor.

- Build AI agents that manage test execution across facilities — initiating runs, monitoring anomalies, implementing test script and firmware changes in response to failures, and routing issues to humans

Test Execution & Reliability Campaigns

- Translate test goals and suspected failure mechanisms into test plans, stress profiles, instrumentation plans, and pass/fail criteria.

- Execute reliability campaigns—burn-in, power cycling, thermal stress, and abuse tests—and evolve them as we learn where the real failure cliffs are.

- Drive fast debug loops during excursions: isolate, instrument deeper, reproduce, and verify that corrective actions eliminate the failure.

What You Will Bring

We prioritize a strong foundation in first principles, practical skill, an inquisitive mindset, and a proactive attitude. We care as much—or more—about how you work as what you already know.

Must-Have Requirements

- Pursuing a BS or MS in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field.

- Hands-on experience designing, building, or operating electrical test setups for complex hardware—power electronics strongly preferred.

- Comfort with bench power equipment and measurement methods: scopes, DMMs, power analyzers, electronic loads, DAQ, and sensors.

- Ability to design safe test systems for high-power hardware: interlocks, protection, grounding, and safe operating procedures.

- Strong debugging instincts and ability to drive root-cause closure with engineering partners.

- Programming experience in Python—including instrument control or data automation.

Nice-to-Haves

- Experience with accelerated or environmental stress testing (HALT/HASS, thermal/humidity cycling, power cycling).

- Familiarity with failure mechanisms in power electronics and structured root cause/corrective action loops.

- Experience designing repeatable test cells with drawings and instructions to turn scrappy setups into production-quality ones.

If you are passionate about technology and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, we would love to hear from you. Join us in accelerating the electrification of everything at Heron Power.

This role combines strategic business analysis, pricing analytics, process mapping, and data visualization. The intern will work cross-functionally with Pricing, Market Access, Finance, Commercial, and Regional teams to establish a sustainable system for measuring the impact of International Pricing activities across the product lifecycle.

Key Responsibilities

Value Measurement Framework Development

- Design a methodology to quantify the value generated through International Pricing recommendations and interventions.
- Develop key performance indicators (KPIs) that measure
- Revenue preservation from pricing strategy decisions
- Value generated through PAR recommendations
- International Reference Pricing (IRP) risk mitigation
- Launch sequencing optimization
- Pricing strategy adoption rates
- Access and reimbursement outcomes influenced by pricing guidance
- Create a repeatable process for measuring realized versus projected impact.

Analytics & Data Management

- Collect and consolidate data from pricing systems, PAR records, forecasts, market submissions, and business cases.
- Develop analytical models to estimate financial and strategic value created by pricing decisions.
- Build dashboards and reports that visualize pricing impact at product, market, regional, and portfolio levels.
- Identify trends and drivers influencing pricing outcomes.

Process Mapping & Improvement

- Map current International Pricing workflows and decision points.
- Identify opportunities to automate data collection and reporting activities.
- Recommend enhancements to improve transparency, consistency, and efficiency in measuring team contributions.
- Document processes and create user guides for future maintenance of the system.

Stakeholder Engagement

- Conduct interviews with International Pricing team members and key stakeholders to understand decision-making processes.
- Gather business requirements and align stakeholders on success metrics.
- Present findings, recommendations, and prototypes to leadership.
- Translate complex pricing concepts into clear business insights.

Final Deliverable

By the conclusion of the internship, the candidate will deliver:

- A documented International Pricing Value Framework
- A KPI dashboard and reporting tool
- A methodology for estimating financial and strategic value creation
- Recommendations for ongoing tracking and governance
- Executive-level presentation summarizing findings and impact

Preferred Project Outcomes

The intern will help answer questions such as:

- How much value has International Pricing created through PAR recommendations?
- What revenue has been protected through IRP risk mitigation?
- How often do pricing recommendations influence final decisions?
- Which pricing interventions have the greatest business impact?
- What metrics best demonstrate the strategic contribution of International Pricing?
- How can value creation be consistently tracked over time?

Success Metrics

A successful intern will:

- Develop a measurable framework accepted by International Pricing leadership.
- Create a sustainable dashboard that can be maintained after the internship.
- Quantify historical and prospective value generated by pricing activities.
- Identify actionable opportunities to improve visibility into pricing decision impact.
- Deliver recommendations that support strategic business decision-making.

Required Qualifications

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Experience with Excel and data analysis.
- Effective written and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to manage multiple projects and work independently.

Preferred

- Experience with Power BI, Tableau, SQL, Python, or R.
- Interest in pharmaceutical pricing, market access, health economics, or healthcare strategy.
- Familiarity with KPI development and business process improvement.
- Experience creating dashboards and executive presentations.

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Firmware Team

The firmware team owns the embedded firmware on all of our microcontroller systems on our aircraft and delivery system. We range from the application layer to the platform and foundation it’s built on. Including bootloaders, RTOS integration, serial and ethernet communication, up to battery management and motor control.

The Role

Zipline aircraft depend on embedded firmware to execute critical flight and safety functions across a network of microcontrollers and embedded Linux computers. This software must perform reliably as aircraft move from manufacturing into delivery operations at field sites around the world, including locations that are difficult to access over a network.

You will own C++ firmware and supporting tools that are critical to the safety and operation of these systems. While making the system more observable and easier to diagnose at scale. Working alongside electrical, mechanical, embedded Linux, and systems engineers, you will turn hardware behavior and flight data into reliable, maintainable software for deployed aircraft.

What You'll Do

- Design and build C++ firmware for a distributed system of aircraft microcontrollers.

- Develop reliable Ethernet, serial, and other microcontroller communication interfaces.

- Define platform-level interfaces and reusable firmware components that support multiple aircraft subsystems.

- Own the predictable and reliable performance of our microcontroller systems and the communication buses that connect them, across startup, real-time operation, fault handling, and recovery.

- Optimize real-time behavior, including CPU utilization, memory usage, scheduling latency, timing jitter, and resource contention

- Develop metrics, monitoring and troubleshooting capabilities to prepare the system for field deployment at scale

- Develop Rust-based tooling and software-in-the-loop simulations to test and validate firmware behavior.

What You'll Bring

You are a person who:

- Is passionate about learning about firmware, realtime systems, Zipline’s aircraft and systems, and our mission.

- Has prior internship or design team experience.

- Has experience with writing C or C++.

- Has excellent grades in embedded systems classes.

It is expected that you will be onsite in South San Francisco 5 days / week for this internship. Rising seniors are preferred.

What Else You Should Know

Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from May to June/September.

Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period.

The hourly rate for this internship is $54 per hour. Job Description:

We are seeking a highly motivated Electrical Design Automation – AI & EDA Automation Intern to help develop next-generation AI-assisted design automation workflows for Signal Integrity (SI) and Power Integrity (PI) engineering.

This internship will focus on applying Large Language Models (LLMs) and Python software development to automate industry-leading Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools, including Ansys HFSS and Keysight ADS. The goal is to create intelligent workflows that transform engineering design specifications and requirements into structured, reusable Python libraries that can automatically generate simulation setups, execute analyses, and produce engineering results.

This project sits at the intersection of electrical engineering, artificial intelligence, software development, and design automation and offers an opportunity to influence the future of engineering productivity and simulation workflows.

Key Responsibilities:

- Develop Python frameworks for automating SI/PI simulation workflows.
- Create structured data models that capture electrical design requirements, constraints, and specifications.
- Investigate and implement LLM-based approaches for translating natural language engineering requirements into machine-readable design objects.
- Interface Python automation with industry-standard EDA tools including:

- Ansys HFSS
- Keysight ADS
- Data analysis and post-processing tools

- Build reusable libraries to support:

- Simulation setup generation
- Parameterized model creation
- Design rule validation
- Results extraction and reporting

- Develop proof-of-concept workflows demonstrating end-to-end automation from specification through simulation execution.
- Collaborate with Signal Integrity and Power Integrity engineers to understand engineering workflows and identify automation opportunities.
- Document software architecture, APIs, and engineering use cases.

Desired Project Outcomes

By the end of the internship, the student will deliver:

- A prototype framework that converts engineering specifications into structured Python objects.
- Demonstration of LLM-assisted specification parsing.
- Automated generation of HFSS and/or ADS simulation projects.
- Workflow examples for SI and PI analysis.
- Documentation and recommendations for future AI-enabled engineering workflows.

Required Qualifications:

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor's, Master's, or Ph.D. degree in:

- Electrical Engineering
- Computer Engineering
- Computer Science
- Applied Physics
- Related technical field

- Strong programming experience in Python.
- Basic understanding of software engineering practices.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Effective verbal and written communication skills.
- Ability to work independently while collaborating with multidisciplinary engineering teams.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Coursework or experience in:

- Signal Integrity
- Power Integrity
- Electromagnetics
- High-speed digital design
- RF engineering

- Experience with one or more EDA tools:

- Ansys HFSS
- Keysight ADS
- Cadence or Synopsys design tools
- Data science and machine learning frameworks

- Familiarity and interest with:

- Object-oriented programming
- Git version control
- Large Language Models (LLMs)
- Prompt engineering
- Agentic AI workflows

- Experience building engineering automation tools is a plus.

What the Intern Will Learn:

- Practical application of AI and LLMs in engineering workflows.
- Automation of commercial EDA tools through Python APIs.
- SI/PI simulation methodologies used in advanced semiconductor test and measurement applications.
- Practical implementation of AI-assisted engineering workflows.

VEHICLE

At American Express, Finance Data Science & Analytics applies advanced modeling, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and statistical techniques to help the organization make scientifically grounded decisions around growth, risk, profitability, and enterprise strategy. Finance Decision Scientists work at the intersection of Finance, Business, Risk, and Technology to develop predictive models, analytical frameworks, and data-driven insights that inform senior management decisions and improve how we forecast, optimize, and manage the business.

This internship is designed for candidates who want to build and apply modeling capabilities to real-world business problems. Interns will work with large-scale datasets, develop and test predictive models, translate business questions into technical modeling approaches, and communicate insights in a clear, structured way. The role requires strong quantitative problem-solving, hands-on programming, and the ability to connect model outputs to business strategy and decision-making.

Team Responsibilities Include:

- Develop predictive models and analytical frameworks that forecast key top-line and financial metrics, supporting both short-term execution and long-term strategic planning.

- Apply machine learning, statistical modeling, and advanced analytics to identify drivers of business performance, risk, customer behavior, and enterprise value.

- Build, validate, and interpret models that inform decisions related to growth, profitability, credit performance, fraud, recessionary preparedness, and balance sheet management.

- Translate complex business problems into structured analytical questions, modeling approaches, and measurable outcomes.

- Partner with Finance, Business, Risk, and Technology teams to embed model-driven insights into strategic decision-making.

- Communicate modeling methodology, assumptions, results, and business implications through clear documentation and executive-ready presentations.

Responsibilities

How will you make an impact in this role?

As an intern your responsibilities can include:

- Query, transform, and analyze large datasets using SQL, Python, and related analytical tools.

- Build, test, and refine predictive models using statistical and machine learning techniques such as regression, classification, clustering, decision trees, and other supervised or unsupervised methods.

- Evaluate model performance, improve predictive accuracy, and document modeling choices, assumptions, limitations, and rationale.

- Apply Python or R to conduct exploratory data analysis, feature engineering, model development, automation, and validation.

- Translate Finance and business objectives into technical requirements, analytical plans, and modeling solutions.

- Develop insights from model outputs and explain implications for business strategy, risk management, financial planning, or operational decision-making.

- Create a clear final presentation that communicates the project’s purpose, modeling approach, key findings, limitations, and business impact.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

- Currently enrolled in a full-time graduate degree program in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Engineering, Quantitative Finance, Artificial Intelligence, Physics, or a related quantitative field.

- Expected graduation date between December 2027 and June 2028.

- Coursework, research, internship, or project experience involving predictive modeling, machine learning, statistical analysis, optimization, or applied data science.

- Demonstrated ability to use programming and quantitative methods to solve ambiguous, real-world problems.

Preferred Qualifications

- Predictive modeling, machine learning, and statistical analysis experience.

- Python or R programming for data analysis, modeling, automation, and validation.

- SQL proficiency and experience working with large datasets.

- Understanding of feature engineering, model training, validation, performance measurement, and interpretation.

- Strong quantitative problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

- Ability to explain modeling approaches and business implications to technical and non-technical audiences.

- Understanding of LLM-based AI systems and the ability to effectively leverage them for optimized workflow

- Power BI or other visualization experience helpful for communicating insights.

FieldAI’s Irvine team is where embodied AI meets real robots, real sensors, and real field deployments. Based in the heart of Southern California’s robotics ecosystem, we build risk-aware, reliable, field-ready AI systems that solve the hardest problems in robotics and unlock the full potential of embodied intelligence. If you want your work to ship, get tested on hardware, and improve through real deployments, Irvine is the place. We go beyond typical data-driven approaches or pure transformer-only architectures, combining rigorous engineering with learning systems proven in globally deployed solutions that deliver results today and get better every time our robots run in the field.

About the Internship

We are offering Spring, Summer, and Fall 2027 research internships in the Irvine office for Master’s and PhD students advancing robotic manipulation.

You will investigate how robots can perform useful physical tasks reliably across diverse objects, environments, and robot platforms. Working closely with researchers and engineers, you will own a focused research project and help translate promising ideas into capabilities that can be tested on hardware and improved through real deployment experience.

Research directions and methods will be shaped by your expertise and the problems we encounter in the field. The goal is to produce original research with measurable impact on what our robots can accomplish.

What We Offer

- Real deployment problems: Work on manipulation challenges grounded in customer use cases and operational needs, with opportunities to evaluate beyond controlled laboratory settings.

- Physical robots and hardware: Develop and validate your work on robotic systems, including humanoids, mobile manipulators, and arm-equipped quadrupeds.

- Research ownership: Shape a focused project, propose your approach, and carry it through implementation, experimentation, and hardware validation.

- Deployment feedback: Use observations and failure cases from real operation to guide research and improve reliability.

- Close technical collaboration: Work with researchers and engineers across robot learning, perception, control, hardware, and deployment.

- Research contributions: Pursue work suitable for leading conferences and journals, with opportunities to release code, datasets, or other research artifacts.

What You Will Get To Do

- Develop manipulation capabilities that address meaningful physical tasks in real environments.

- Investigate how skills transfer across objects, tasks, environments, and robot platforms.

- Address practical challenges such as uncertainty, contact, changing conditions, and failure recovery.

- Design experiments that measure task success, generalization, and reliability under realistic operating conditions.

- Integrate and validate research on physical robots, collaborating with engineering teams to address system constraints.

- Document findings, present results, and contribute to publications or reusable research tools.

What You Have

- Current master’s or PhD enrollment in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, AI/ML, or a closely related field.

- Research experience in robotic manipulation, robot learning, embodied AI, or a related area.

- A strong research or open-source track record, demonstrated through substantive publications, research software, or technically rigorous projects.

- Clear ownership of original research or technical development, including implementation and evaluation.

- Strong foundations in robotics, machine learning, and experimental design.

- Proficiency in Python and/or C++.

- Ability to work independently, communicate findings clearly, and collaborate across research and engineering disciplines.

The Extras That Set You Apart

- First-author publications at venues such as RSS, CoRL, ICRA, IROS, NeurIPS, ICLR, or ICML, or journals such as RA-L, T-RO, or IJRR.

- Significant contributions to open-source robotics or machine learning projects with demonstrated adoption.

- Hands-on experience taking research from an initial idea to reliable operation on physical robots.

- Experience evaluating robotic systems outside controlled laboratory conditions.

- Public research code, datasets, or robot demonstrations showing technical depth and measurable results.

- Experience with robot integration, sensing, control, or data collection infrastructure.

Our salary range is generous and we consider each individual’s background and experience when determining final compensation. Base pay may vary based on role scope, job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and the Irvine, California market.

Why Join FieldAI in Irvine?

In Irvine, you will work where the robots are. Our local team builds and tests systems on real hardware with real sensors, then ships them to operate in unstructured, previously unknown environments around the world. We are solving one of robotics’ hardest challenges: reliable deployment outside the lab. Our Field Foundational Models™ raise the bar for perception, planning, localization, and manipulation, with an emphasis on explainability and safety for real-world use.

You will collaborate with a world-class team that thrives on creativity, resilience, and bold thinking. We bring deep experience from organizations such as DeepMind, NASA JPL, Boston Dynamics, NVIDIA, Amazon, Tesla Autopilot, Cruise, Zoox, Toyota Research Institute, and SpaceX, along with a track record of field deployments and strong performance in DARPA challenge segments.

Be Part of the Next Robotics Revolution

We are looking for builders who want their work to leave the whiteboard and show up on robots. If you enjoy tackling tough, uncharted questions and working across disciplines, you will find your people here. Our teams span AI, software, robotics engineering, product, field deployment, and technical communication, all focused on shipping systems that perform in the real world.

Our headquarters is in Irvine, and we partner closely with teams there as well as colleagues across the US and around the world. Join us in Southern California and help define what dependable, field-ready autonomy looks like.

We value diverse perspectives and are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace. We evaluate candidates and employees based on merit, qualifications, and performance, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, or any other legally protected status.

POSITION SUMMARY:

At National Life Group, we are unlocking the power of data and AI to transform our business and enhance customer experience. Our AI Center of Excellence (AICoE) is leading this effort through innovations in machine learning, advanced analytics, and generative AI.

As a Data Science Intern, you will contribute to projects within our AI CoE. You’ll gain hands-on experience applying computer science and data science techniques to real business challenges. Projects may range from supporting the development of predictive models to testing and enhancing generative AI solutions.

This is a unique opportunity to explore both traditional data science methods and emerging AI technologies while working in a collaborative, mission-driven environment.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

In this role, you will collaborate with AI and data science practitioners, technical experts, and business partners. You will work primarily in National Life’s Databricks environment to develop and evaluate data-driven solutions. Depending on project priorities, responsibilities may include:

- Prepare, explore, and validate datasets and features for life insurance and annuity use cases such as surrender propensity, premium persistency, and policyholder behavioral analysis.

- Support the development and evaluation of statistical and machine-learning models, comparing results with established baselines and investigating errors and limitations.

- Help design experiments and analyze business outcomes using appropriate comparisons, sound statistical methods, and clear measures of success.

- Develop reusable Python and SQL workflows, including validation checks and documentation that allow others to review and reproduce the work.

- Prototype and evaluate generative AI applications, assessing output quality, source support, failure modes, and practical business usefulness.

- Apply responsible AI and data-handling practices, including appropriate treatment of sensitive information and validation of AI-generated outputs.

- Communicate findings and recommendations to technical and business audiences.

- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, data science, mathematics, statistics, or a related field.

- Strong programming skills in Python, with experience using data analysis or machine-learning libraries such as pandas and scikit-learn. Exposure to Apache Spark, PyTorch, or TensorFlow is a plus.

- Working knowledge of SQL, including querying, joining, and aggregating data to prepare and validate datasets for analysis and modeling.

- Familiarity with foundational statistical and machine-learning concepts, including regression, classification, model evaluation, and hypothesis testing.

- Coursework or projects integrating generative AI APIs into software is a plus.

- Curiosity and eagerness to learn about the real-world application of both modern AI technologies and foundational statistical methods.

- Strong communication skills and ability to work collaboratively in a team environment.

- Use AI responsibly and in accordance with company policies related to confidentiality, data privacy, security, compliance, retention, and intellectual property.

Founded in 2023, Mach Industries is a rapidly growing defense technology company focused on developing next-generation autonomous defense platforms. At the core of our mission is the commitment to delivering scalable, decentralized defense systems that enhance the strategic capabilities of the United States and its allies. Our vision is to redefine the future of warfare through cutting-edge manufacturing, innovation at speed, and unwavering focus on national security. We are dedicated to solving the next generation of warfare with lethal systems that deter kinetic conflict and protect global security.

The Role

Mach Industries is seeking a New Graduate Electrical & Avionics Engineer to support the design, development, integration, and testing of electrical systems for next-generation autonomous defense platforms. In this role, you will work across circuit-board design, avionics, power distribution, communications, vehicle harnessing, and hardware testing to take systems from early prototypes through flight-ready production hardware.

You will collaborate closely with mechanical, software, systems, manufacturing, and test engineers to rapidly build, troubleshoot, and validate reliable electrical systems. This role is ideal for a hands-on engineer who wants broad technical ownership, learns quickly, and is excited to build critical hardware in a fast-paced environment.

Key Responsibilities

- Design and develop electrical and avionics systems for autonomous aircraft, missiles, propulsion systems, and related defense platforms.

- Design and integrate vehicle wiring harnesses, connectors, sensors, actuators, and electrical interfaces.

- Build prototypes and conduct bench-level, subsystem, and vehicle-level testing using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, power supplies, electronic loads, and other laboratory equipment.

- Troubleshoot electrical hardware, identify root causes, and implement design or process improvements.

- Develop and maintain schematics, drawings, bills of materials, test procedures, design documentation, and product specifications.

- Partner with mechanical, software, systems, manufacturing, and test teams to ensure electrical components integrate successfully into the overall vehicle.

- Work alongside manufacturing and quality teams to transition designs from prototype builds into reliable, repeatable production.

- Ensure designs meet applicable performance, reliability, safety, quality, and regulatory requirements.

- Bachelor’s, master’s, or doctoral degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical field.

- Graduating by December 2026

- Electrical or avionics experience gained through internships, research, academic projects, student competition teams, or professional roles.

- Foundational understanding of analog and digital electronics, circuit design, power systems, and electrical interfaces.

- Experience with schematic capture or PCB design software such as Altium Designer, Cadence, KiCad, or an equivalent tool.

- Hands-on experience building, testing, debugging, or integrating electrical hardware.

- Ability to work effectively across engineering disciplines in a fast-paced, hardware-focused environment.

- Experience designing, assembling, or testing printed circuit boards.

- Experience with microcontrollers, embedded systems, sensors, actuators, communications buses, or power-distribution systems.

- Familiarity with common communication protocols such as CAN, Ethernet, USB, SPI, I2C, UART, or MIPI.

- Experience with vehicle harnessing, connector selection, wiring diagrams, or electrical system integration.

- Participation in technical organizations or student teams such as Formula SAE, Design/Build/Fly, rocketry, robotics, UAV, CubeSat, or autonomous vehicle teams.

- Experience using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, multimeters, power supplies, electronic loads, or other electrical test equipment.

- Familiarity with high-speed digital design, signal integrity, power integrity, EMI/EMC, grounding, and circuit protection.

- Exposure to embedded programming in C, C++, Python, or a related language.

Parallel Systems is pioneering autonomous battery-electric rail vehicles designed to transform freight transportation by shifting portions of the $900 billion U.S. trucking industry onto rail. Our innovative technology offers cleaner, safer, and more efficient logistics solutions. Join our dynamic team and help shape a smarter, greener future for global freight.

Software Engineering Interns

Parallel Systems is seeking Software Engineering Interns to help build the software that runs our vehicles and the platform behind our fleet. This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to ship real work. Your code will run on prototype vehicles, on test benches, or in the services and tools our team and operators rely on every day.

Interns are placed on a vehicle software or backend/full-stack project based on their background and team priorities. You will own a scoped project from requirements through delivery, work closely with a mentor, and see your work tested on real hardware or used by real users.

The right person is curious beyond their own layer. Whether you are writing firmware, building a service, or shipping an internal tool, you will learn how software, hardware, and vehicle data fit together, and you will be comfortable debugging across those boundaries.

What You Will Work On

You will contribute to a specific project scoped to team priorities. Example areas include:

- Vehicle control software: writing and testing code for braking, drivetrain, actuators, and power systems on microcontrollers or embedded Linux

- Vehicle communications: developing and validating interfaces across CAN, Ethernet, SPI, I2C, or UART, including bench debugging

- Sensor and diagnostics integration: bringing up onboard sensors and devices used for telemetry, health monitoring, and vehicle operation

- Fleet and telemetry services: building services and data pipelines that ingest, store, and serve data from vehicles in the field

- Fleet operations tools: building APIs and web applications used to monitor, dispatch, and manage vehicles

- Developer and test infrastructure: improving CI/CD, simulation, hardware-in-the-loop testing, deployment, and observability for the software team

Regardless of project, you will work through a structured engineering lifecycle: requirements review, design, implementation, testing, and documentation of results.

What to Expect

- Weeks 1-2: Onboarding, vehicle and software platform architecture overview, development environment setup, lab and shop orientation, codebase familiarization, and a first starter task

- Weeks 3-4: Project assignment, review of requirements and interfaces, and initial design and debugging work with your mentor

- Weeks 5-7: Core implementation, testing on the bench or in staging, and iteration through code and design reviews

- Weeks 8-10: Integration onto prototype vehicles or into production systems, test execution, issue investigation, and participation in team design reviews

- Weeks 11-12: Final validation and handoff, documentation of findings and recommended next steps, and a presentation of results to the broader engineering team

Progress will be tracked through weekly check-ins with your mentor, design and code reviews, and feedback from the broader engineering team.

Basic Requirements

- Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Mechatronics, or a related field

- Hands-on software experience through internships, student teams, research, coursework, or personal projects

- Strong programming skills in at least one language such as Rust, C, C++, Python, Go, or TypeScript

- A track record of building software that works in the real world, not only in class assignments or simulation

- Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to debug issues across system boundaries

- Clear communication, and comfort asking questions and sharing progress early

- Excitement about working in a hands-on, hard-tech environment where software meets physical vehicles

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with Rust, C, or C++ on microcontrollers or embedded Linux

- Familiarity with communication protocols such as CAN, SPI, I2C, UART, or Ethernet

- Experience building APIs, distributed services, data pipelines, or full-stack web applications

- Familiarity with databases, cloud infrastructure, containers, or CI/CD

- Exposure to RTOS environments, simulation, or hardware-in-the-loop testing

- Experience bringing up sensors, actuators, motor controllers, or other real electromechanical systems

- Experience from hands-on extracurricular engineering teams such as Formula SAE, Baja SAE, robotics, rocket club, solar car, autonomous systems teams, or similar

- Strong documentation habits and attention to detail

Build your first real systems engineering experience on AI hardware you can measure, test and improve.

You will join systems engineers who work across hardware, firmware, software, mechanical and thermal teams. Work happens through lab measurement, script-driven validation, shared debugging and clear engineering notes.

You will be given defined problems to own, with guidance from engineers who expect curiosity and careful thinking. Decisions are made through data, reproducible results and open technical review.

Navi captures everything a pilot sees and hears and turns it into automated debrief intelligence — sortie-level awareness that has never existed before. None of it works without the hardware in the aircraft. That's what you'll build.

About the role

This is a hands-on hardware internship. You'll build, test, and ship the devices that fly in real aircraft at university flight schools and military squadrons. Every unit you assemble ends up in a cockpit, capturing data a pilot and instructor will sit down and review that same day. Nothing here is a prototype exercise. Navi is already live at leading flight schools.

You'll work directly with our hardware and engineering teams, and you'll see the consequences of your work fast — if a unit fails, you'll hear about it, and you'll be part of fixing it.

What you'll do

- Assemble, wire, and bench-test Navi devices — audio capture, mounting hardware, cable harnesses, enclosures

- Diagnose failures on returned or field-reported units and feed what you learn back into the build

- Help improve the build itself — fixturing, assembly documentation, anything that makes the next hundred units faster and more reliable than the last hundred

- Track inventory, components, and BOMs so we never stall a deployment waiting on a part

- Assist in preparing shipments, and willing to learn and assist in other tasks too

- Work alongside engineers across hardware, firmware, and software to close the loop between what we build and what pilots actually experience

About you

- Currently pursuing a degree in engineering, or equivalent hands-on experience — we care more about what you've built than where you're enrolled

- Comfortable with hand tools, wiring and basic electronics debugging

- Careful and consistent. Hardware that flies has to be built the same way every time, and you take that seriously

- You've built physical things — personal projects, robotics teams, Formula SAE, RC aircraft, drones, a workshop in your garage. Tell us about them

- Willing to do the unglamorous work. Some days are assembly and testing, and those units still have to be perfect

- Curious about why things fail and persistent enough to find out

- Comfortable in ambiguity — processes here are still being written, and you'll help write them

Nice to have

- You know how to fly. A private pilot certificate, student pilot time, or any flight training is a real bonus. Pilots understand the cockpit environment these devices live in, and we'll lean on you for more than device build — flight testing, data collection, ride-alongs, and translating what actually happens in the aircraft back to the engineering team

- Familiarity with aviation systems, avionics, or general aviation aircraft

- CAD, 3D printing, or fabrication experience

- Basic scripting for test automation or data validation

Why this role matters

Pilots trust their lives to the systems in front of them. The device you build is the first link in that chain — if it doesn't capture clean data, nothing downstream works. Interns here own real units going to real customers, not side projects.

What you'll get

- Hardware that ships — your work flies in aircraft at flight schools, airlines, and the U.S. Air Force

- Direct access to the founding team and every part of the stack, from hardware to AI

- A path to a full-time role for interns who prove they can own the build

How we work

- Find a way. We don't wait for permission or perfect information. Ideas come from anywhere regardless of title. Figure it out, ship it, iterate.

- Creativity over control. First principles over process. We'd rather have a creative solution that's 80% right today than a perfect one next quarter.

- Update fast. Come in with a hypothesis, throw it away when the data says otherwise. Ego has no place here.

- Intensity with focus. We work hard because the mission demands it. Clarity on what matters is how we make that sustainable.

Join the team bringing advanced autonomy to the built world

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and into the real world. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. Today, we're deploying autonomous systems on heavy construction equipment across the country, improving safety on job sites and accelerating schedules on critical infrastructure projects.

We're not here debating the future of AI. We're deploying it in the real world. In just two years, we've raised $350M and achieved the first fully autonomous excavator deployments in construction.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.

About the Role & Team

Bedrock's Product team decides what our autonomous machines should learn to do next. We also make sure the people who work alongside them get real value from them: operators, site managers and the construction companies we partner with. Our problems rarely arrive as specs. Which task or machine type is worth taking on next? How do you turn "digs like an expert" into a number you can measure? What does a partner need to see before trusting a 40-ton machine on their site?

As our Product intern, you'll get a problem like that, not a task list, and own it for the summer. You'll frame it, work out the answer, build what's needed, and bring the team a recommendation they can act on. You'll work the way our team does: with AI tools in hand, going from question to working prototype in days, not weeks.

What You'll Do

- Own an open product problem end to end: frame it, find the data and the people who know, decide what to build, and ship it before the summer ends

- Turn fleet data from real jobsites into decisions: how well our machines perform, where they struggle, and what that means for what we build next

- Prototype with AI coding tools and agents: internal tools, data pipelines, automated workflows, and working demos that make an idea concrete instead of slides about it

- Spend time at our field sites with operators and site teams, and turn what you see into requirements engineers can build against

- Work across autonomy, evaluation, operations and commercial teams to pressure-test ideas and unblock yourself

- Write up your findings and present a clear recommendation to leadership: what you found, what you built, and what we should do next

What We're Looking For

Required

- Currently pursuing a BS or MS in computer science, engineering, math, economics or another technical or quantitative field, or bringing equivalent experience building things

- A track record of agency: you've taken on a problem nobody assigned you (a project, a tool, a company, a research question) and carried it to a real result

- AI-native: you use tools like Claude Code, Cursor or Codex every day to build, analyze and write, and you know how to check their output and when not to trust it

- Hands-on with data: Python or SQL, plus comfort reading code and following a technical discussion with engineers

- Clear, concise writing: you can turn a messy problem into a one-page recommendation someone can act on

- Willingness to spend time at our field sites, in PPE, around heavy equipment

Preferred

- Something you built that real people use: an app, an internal tool, an open-source project, a startup

- Prior product, engineering or founding-team experience at a startup

- Experience with robotics, autonomy, ML or data-heavy products

- Interest in construction or other physical-world industries; no prior experience needed

About This Internship

This is a fixed-term, project-based internship designed strictly for students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. Please note that while exceptional interns may occasionally be considered if business needs align, opportunities for full-time conversion are highly limited."

In this role, you will work primarily with the Business Intelligence team to support reporting, analysis, and automation initiatives in a structured learning environment. Your day may include working with sample or curated datasets, building Excel-based models or trackers, developing Power BI dashboards, writing SQL queries, and assisting with data pipeline and workflow automation tasks. You may also support recurring reporting processes, help document business rules and reporting logic, investigate data quality patterns in non-production datasets, and contribute to lightweight Azure-based integrations and process improvements.

This is a hands-on internship where you will gain exposure to both business intelligence and data engineering work. You will learn how data moves across systems, how dashboards and reports are built for business users, and how automation can improve speed, accuracy, and scalability across core processes.

Key Responsibilities

- Assist in the development and maintenance of Power BI dashboards and reports to support business and operational insights

- Support data preparation activities, including data cleaning, transformation, and validation using Power Query and SQL

- Help connect and integrate data from multiple sources, such as databases, spreadsheets, and business systems, into Power BI

- Create and maintain basic DAX measures and calculations under guidance from senior analysts

- Assist with data modeling tasks, including building and validating relationships and tables used for reporting

- Write SQL queries in Azure SQL Database to support reporting, data validation, and business analysis

- Help create and maintain automated workflows in Power Automate for notifications, approvals, and recurring business processes

- Support lightweight integrations and automation using Azure Functions where applicable

- Perform data quality checks and help identify data inconsistencies or anomalies

- Support documentation of report definitions, data sources, data models, business logic, and workflow steps

- Learn and follow BI best practices related to data governance, security, and reporting standards

Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Data Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Analytics, Engineering, or a related field

- Familiarity with Power BI, Power Query, and DAX

- Experience using Excel for data analysis, such as PivotTables, formulas, charts, lookups, and basic dashboards

- Power Automate skills, such as flows, connectors, approvals, scheduled and event-based triggers, conditions, loops, integrations, and error handling

- Azure SQL Database skills, such as writing queries, working with tables and views, joins, aggregations, stored procedures, triggers, and query optimization

- Azure Data Factory skills, such as linked services, datasets, copy activities, pipeline development, triggers, parameterization, monitoring, and error handling

- Azure Functions skills, such as Function Apps, triggers, bindings, service integrations, logging, troubleshooting, and serverless design

- Familiarity with databases, data warehouses, or ETL concepts from classes, projects, or internships

- Comfortable working with structured and imperfect data, with the ability to identify inconsistencies, improve data quality, learn new tools quickly, and operate effectively in a fast-paced environment

- Interest in building scalable, reliable data solutions that support better business decisions

Internship experience and compensation

This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges form $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. Interns participate in Early Career programming, including technical and professional-development sessions, community events, and an end-of-program project presentation.

We know that creativity and innovation happen more often when teams include diverse ideas, backgrounds, and experiences, and we actively encourage everyone with relevant experience to apply, including people of color, LGBTQ+ and non-binary people, veterans, parents, and individuals with disabilities.
